items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 39:1
items.html: Turneya means 'crown,' and this Hesed that is revealed at the mouth of the Yesod of Atik is called Turneya Basima Y'ai. It is called Basima ('sweetened') because it sweetens the Gevurot and tempers them. And it is called Y'ai ('beautiful') on account of the revelation of the illumination of Hochma in its Hassadim, which is beauty, as in the verse 'and Joseph was of beautiful form,' for the wisdom of a man illumines his face. And the Zohar says in Idra Zuta: 'The forehead that is revealed is called Will, for RADLA extends a certain Turneya Basima Y'ai that is included in the forehead.' Meaning: the NHY of Atik that are clothed in the Mochin of Arich Anpin are divided into nine Sefirot — HBD, HGT, NHY — and are likewise divided into MEM-LAMED-TZADIK. The aspect of the MEM in them, which is the two upper joints of Atik above the Yesod, being the aspect of HBD, are clothed in the ears and the forehead; and the upper joint of the Yesod of Atik is found concealed in the forehead of Arich Anpin, while the lower joint, called the corona, is clothed in the nose of Arich Anpin. And it is known that in the MEM of Tzelem the Yud does not go out of the air, and it always remains in concealed Hassadim; hence the Yesod of Atik is called there by the language of concealment, for the light of Hesed in it is concealed and covered, and the revelation of the illumination of Hochma does not operate there. But in the LAMED of Tzelem, which are the two eyes and the nose, there is the place of the revelation of Hochma in Hassadim, for there the Yud goes out of the air and light remains, as is known. Hence the place of the revelation of the Hassadim is the corona of the Yesod of Atik, clothed in the nose of Arich Anpin. Therefore the Zohar calls this illumination of the revelation of Hochma in Hassadim 'Turneya,' meaning a crown, for there is no revelation of Hassadim in the Yesod of Atik that is clothed in the forehead, but only in the corona of Atik that is clothed in the nose, which is called the mouth of the Yesod. And since all the illumination of the corona of the Yesod is included in the Yesod, therefore, although there is no revelation in the Yesod itself, the power of the revelation of the corona ascends to it from below upward of its own accord. Hence, by the power of the revelation of this illumination, the forehead is then called 'the forehead of will,' by virtue of the illumination of this Turneya Basima Y'ai that is included in it, as written in the Zohar. Understand this, for it does not say that the Turneya Basima Y'ai is revealed in it — because in the forehead itself there is no revelation of Hassadim, since the Yesod is concealed there — but rather it says that this Turneya Basima Y'ai is included in it. That is, as explained: the illumination of the corona of the Yesod ascends and shines in the Yesod that is in the forehead from below upward, since the Yesod is the root of this light revealed in the corona, and all the illuminations of the corona are included in the Yesod, as explained. And with this you will understand that the light of the forehead itself is the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem, which is the first three of Bina, which longs for Hassadim more than for Hochma, in the secret of 'for He delights in mercy.' And after this light of Hesed the forehead is called 'the forehead of will,' for 'will' (ratzon) is the letters of 'keeps' (notzer), being the aspect of 'for He delights in mercy,' as written in the Zohar that this illumination reaches the upper Mazal of the beard, called 'and He keeps mercy.' But the will is not revealed in the forehead before this Turneya Basima Y'ai is extended, for by virtue of its inclusion in it, the will is revealed in the Hesed that is in the forehead. Understand this well. (Page 338, Items 87-88).
